ex: Папа ends in -а but means a man, so it is masculine: мой папа.
translation: This is my dad.

ex: Мама is feminine (ends in -а), so use моя.
translation: This is my mom.

ex: Письмо is neuter (ends in -о), so use моё.
translation: Where is my letter?

ex: Книги is plural, so use мои.
translation: These are my books.

ex: Сестра is feminine, so твой becomes твоя.
translation: Your sister lives in Moscow.

ex: Дом is masculine (ends in a consonant), so наш stays наш.
translation: This is our house.

ex: Чей (whose) agrees with the noun. Машина is feminine: чья машина?
translation: Whose car is this?

ex: Adjectives match the noun. Машина is feminine: новая.
translation: I have a new car.

ex: Город is masculine, so the adjective keeps the -ый ending.
translation: This is a very beautiful city.

ex: Погода is feminine: хорошая. (The neuter form is хорошее, never хорошое.)
translation: The weather is nice today.

ex: Окно is neuter (ends in -о), so the adjective takes -ое.
translation: This is a big window.

ex: Соседи is plural, so the adjective takes -ые.
translation: We have new neighbors.

ex: The adjective matches город (masculine), not Москва.
translation: Moscow is a very big city.

ex: Телефон ends in a consonant, so it is masculine: он (it).
translation: Where's my phone? — Here it is.

ex: Сумка ends in -а, so it is feminine: она (it).
translation: Where's my bag? — Here it is.

ex: Пальто ends in -о, so it is neuter: оно (it). Пальто never changes its ending.
translation: Where's your coat? — Here it is.

ex: Ключи is plural: они (they).
translation: Where are the keys? — Here they are.

ex: Друг has an irregular plural: друзья.
translation: These are my friends.

ex: Feminine -а nouns take -ы in the plural, but after г, к, х, ж, ш, щ, ч you write -и: книги.
translation: There are books on the table.

ex: Some masculine nouns take a stressed -а in the plural: дома, города.
translation: There are new buildings in our neighborhood.

ex: Most masculine nouns add -ы in the plural: студенты.
translation: Students are sitting in the classroom.

ex: After ч (and г, к, х, ж, ш, щ) the plural ending is -и, never -ы.
translation: Where are my keys?

ex: Ребёнок has an irregular plural: дети.
translation: My kids love soccer.

ex: Nouns ending in a soft sign take -и in the plural: родитель → родители.
translation: My parents live in Minsk.

ex: Location (where?) uses в/на + prepositional. Most nouns take -е: в Москве.
translation: I live in Moscow.

ex: На + prepositional for location. Masculine nouns add -е: на столе.
translation: The book is on the table.

ex: В + prepositional answers 'where?': в парке.
translation: We're in the park right now.

ex: Feminine -а nouns change -а to -е in the prepositional: в больнице.
translation: My mom works in a hospital.

ex: В + prepositional: университет → в университете.
translation: My brother studies at the university.

ex: Events use на: на концерте, на работе, на уроке.
translation: Yesterday we were at a concert.

ex: О (about) + prepositional: о работе.
translation: I often think about work.

ex: Nouns in -ия take -ии (not -ие) in the prepositional: в России.
translation: Have you been to Russia?

ex: A direct object goes in the accusative. Feminine -а becomes -у: книгу.
translation: I'm reading a book.

ex: Любить + accusative: -а → -у.
translation: I really love music.

ex: Direct object, feminine: вода → воду.
translation: She's drinking water.

ex: Видеть + accusative: Анна → Анну.
translation: I see Anna.

ex: Masculine nouns for things don't change in the accusative: смотреть фильм.
translation: In the evening we watch a movie.

ex: Masculine nouns for people or animals add -а in the accusative: Ивана.
translation: Do you know Ivan?

ex: В + accusative answers 'where to?': в школу. В + prepositional answers 'where?': в школе.
translation: I'm going to school now.

ex: Кино is a borrowed word and never changes its ending: в кино, о кино.
translation: We're going to the movies tonight.

ex: 'I have' is у меня есть (literally 'by me there is'). У takes the genitive: меня.
translation: I have a brother.

ex: У + genitive: ты → тебя.
translation: Do you have a car?

ex: After a preposition, он/она/они get an н-: у него, у неё, у них.
translation: He has a dog.

ex: Нет (there is no) + genitive. Feminine -а → -ы: машины.
translation: I don't have a car.

ex: Нет + genitive. Masculine nouns add -а: хлеба.
translation: Sorry, we don't have any bread.

ex: Нет + genitive. Neuter -о → -а: молока.
translation: There's no milk in the store.

ex: 'Mom's bag' is сумка мамы: the owner goes in the genitive, after the thing.
translation: This is Mom's bag.

ex: Russian says 'Moscow is pleasing to me': the person who likes goes in the dative (мне).
translation: I like Moscow.

ex: Нравится + dative: тебе.
translation: Do you like this movie?

ex: Надо (need to) takes the person in the dative: ему надо.
translation: He needs to work.

ex: Нравится + dative. Feminine -а → -е: Анне.
translation: Anna likes music.

ex: Звонить (to call) + dative. Masculine nouns add -у: брату.
translation: I'm calling my brother.

ex: Надо + dative: мы → нам.
translation: It's late already; we need to go.

ex: С (with) + instrumental. Neuter -о nouns add -м: с молоком.
translation: I drink tea with milk.

ex: С + instrumental. Feminine -а → -ой: с мамой.
translation: I live with my mom.

ex: С + instrumental: собака → собакой.
translation: In the morning I walk the dog.
glosses: гулять: to go for a walk

ex: С + instrumental. Masculine nouns add -ом: с другом.
translation: I go to the movies with a friend.

ex: С + instrumental: мы → нами.
translation: Do you want to come with us?

ex: Любить + accusative: ты → тебя.
translation: I love you.

ex: Знать + accusative: она → её. (Ней is used only after a preposition.)
translation: Do you know her?

ex: Звонить/позвонить + dative: вы → вам.
translation: I'll call you tomorrow.

ex: Видеть + accusative: он → его. (Него is used only after a preposition.)
translation: Where's Ivan? I don't see him.

ex: 2nd conjugation (most -ить verbs): я говорю, ты говоришь, он говорит, мы говорим, вы говорите, они говорят.
translation: I speak Russian.

ex: 2nd conjugation: ты говоришь (-ишь).
translation: Do you speak English?

ex: 1st conjugation (most -ать verbs): я читаю, ты читаешь, он читает, мы читаем, вы читаете, они читают.
translation: I'm reading an interesting book.

ex: 1st conjugation: мы работаем (-ем).
translation: We work at a bank.

ex: 1st conjugation: они слушают (-ют).
translation: They often listen to music.

ex: 1st conjugation: вы делаете (-ете).
translation: What are you doing on Saturday?

ex: 1st conjugation: он понимает (-ет).
translation: He understands Russian well.

ex: Смотреть is 2nd conjugation: мы смотрим (-им).
translation: In the evening we watch TV.

ex: 2nd conjugation: они сидят (-ят).
translation: They're sitting in a café.

ex: Любить: я люблю (an л is added in the я-form), ты любишь.
translation: I really love coffee.

ex: Спать: я сплю, ты спишь, он спит, они спят.
translation: Are you still asleep?

ex: Жить adds в: я живу, ты живёшь, он живёт, мы живём, вы живёте, они живут.
translation: I live in Minsk.

ex: Жить: вы живёте.
translation: Where do you live?

ex: Хотеть: я хочу, ты хочешь, он хочет (т → ч in the singular).
translation: I want tea.

ex: Хотеть: мы хотим, вы хотите, они хотят (no ч in the plural).
translation: Would you like coffee?

ex: Есть (to eat): я ем, ты ешь, он ест, мы едим, вы едите, они едят.
translation: I don't eat meat.

ex: Есть: ты ешь. Don't confuse it with едешь (from ехать, to ride).
translation: What do you eat for lunch?

ex: Мочь (can): я могу, ты можешь, он может, мы можем, вы можете, они могут.
translation: Can you help me?

ex: Мочь: мы можем.
translation: Sorry, we can't come.

ex: The past tense agrees with the subject: он был, она была, оно было, они были.
translation: Yesterday Ivan was at home.

ex: Feminine subject: была.
translation: Anna was in Moscow in May.

ex: Plural subjects (мы, вы, они): были.
translation: We were at the movies on Saturday.

ex: Sentences with no subject (холодно, жарко) use the neuter: было.
translation: It was very cold yesterday.

ex: Ты here is Маша, a woman, so the past tense is feminine: ты была.
translation: Masha, where were you yesterday?

ex: Feminine past: -ла. Мама готовила.
translation: Mom made a delicious soup.

ex: Masculine past: -л. Папа читал.
translation: In the morning Dad read the newspaper.

ex: Plural past: -ли. Дети играли.
translation: The kids played in the park all day.

ex: Прийти has an irregular past: пришёл, пришла, пришло, пришли. Письмо is neuter: пришло.
translation: Your letter arrived yesterday.

ex: Мы takes the plural past: смотрели.
translation: Yesterday we watched a good movie.

ex: Идти (to go on foot): я иду, ты идёшь, он идёт, мы идём, вы идёте, они идут.
translation: I'm walking home now.

ex: Идти: ты идёшь.
translation: Where are you going?

ex: Ехать (to go by vehicle): я еду, ты едешь, он едет, мы едем, вы едете, они едут.
translation: We're going to Moscow by train.

ex: Ехать: они едут.
translation: They're going to work by bus.

ex: Пешком means on foot, so use идти.
translation: He's walking to the store.

ex: By car, bus, or train you use ехать, not идти.
translation: I'm driving to Minsk.

ex: The present tense of ехать can describe a planned trip: завтра я еду. (Поеду also works.)
translation: Tomorrow I'm going to St. Petersburg.

ex: Где asks 'where?' (location). Куда asks 'where to?' (direction).
translation: Where do you live?

ex: With motion verbs (идти, ехать) ask куда (where to).
translation: Where are you going?

ex: Домой means (to) home, with motion. Дома means at home (location).
translation: I'm going home now.

ex: Ходила means went (and came back). Past tense, feminine: -ла.
translation: Yesterday Masha went to the theater.

s: Я часто думаю о ___ после нашего разговора.
ex: О + prepositional. Masculine hard-stem nouns take -е: о брате.
translation: I often think about my brother after our conversation.

s: На совещании мы долго говорили о ___ компании.
ex: Будущее declines like a neuter adjective. Prepositional singular: -ем (о будущем).
translation: At the meeting we talked for a long time about the company's future.

s: Моя жена работает в ___ при университете.
ex: Nouns in -ия take -ии in the prepositional (and genitive, dative): в лаборатории, not *лабораторие.
translation: My wife works in a laboratory at the university.

ex: Some masculine nouns take stressed -у after в/на for location (locative): в Крыму, в лесу, в аэропорту.
translation: Last summer we vacationed in Crimea.

s: Ключи от машины лежат на ___ в прихожей.
ex: Шкаф has the locative -у after в/на: на шкафу, в шкафу (like на полу, в углу).
translation: The car keys are on the wardrobe in the hallway.

s: Извини, сегодня у меня совсем нет ___.
ex: Нет + genitive. Neuter nouns in -мя add -ен-: время → времени (like имя → имени).
translation: Sorry, I have no time at all today.

s: Это машина моего ___, он дал мне её на выходные.
ex: Possession = genitive. Masculine nouns in -я decline like feminine ones: дядя → дяди.
translation: This is my uncle's car; he lent it to me for the weekend.

ex: After много/мало/несколько the genitive plural of человек is людей. The form человек is used only after numerals and сколько: пять человек.
translation: There were a lot of people at the conference.

s: К сожалению, в нашем районе нет хороших ___.
ex: Нет + genitive plural. Masculine hard-stem nouns take -ов: ресторанов.
translation: Unfortunately, there are no good restaurants in our neighborhood.

ex: After 5+ use the genitive plural. Neuter nouns in -о usually have a zero ending: яблоко → яблок.
translation: Please buy six apples for the pie.

s: В нашем новом офисе очень мало ___.
ex: Мало + genitive plural. Neuter -о nouns take a zero ending, often with an inserted vowel: окно → окон.
translation: There are very few windows in our new office.

s: Подожди меня, пожалуйста, мне нужно ещё пять ___.
ex: After пять and higher: genitive plural. Feminine -а nouns take a zero ending: минута → минут.
translation: Please wait for me, I need five more minutes.

s: До зарплаты ещё неделя, а у меня уже нет ___.
ex: Деньги is plural-only. Its genitive is денег (with an inserted -е-, no -ов).
translation: It's still a week until payday, and I'm already out of money.

s: Сколько у вас ___ отпуска в году?
ex: Сколько + genitive plural. Feminine nouns in -я after a consonant drop the ending and keep a soft sign: неделя → недель.
translation: How many weeks of vacation do you get a year?

s: В этом журнале много интересных ___ о науке.
ex: Nouns in -ья have the genitive plural -ей: статья → статей (like семья → семей).
translation: There are many interesting articles about science in this magazine.

s: Вчера вечером я позвонил ___ и рассказал про новую работу.
ex: Звонить + dative (to call someone). Feminine -а nouns take -е: маме.
translation: Last night I called Mom and told her about my new job.

ex: With нравиться, the person who likes something is in the dative. Plural: -им (possessive/adjective) + -ям/-ам (noun).
translation: My parents didn't like this movie at all.

s: По вечерам я люблю гулять по ___.
ex: По (along, around) + dative. Набережная declines like a feminine adjective: dative -ой.
translation: In the evenings I like to walk along the embankment.

ex: In impersonal constructions with нужно/надо/можно, the person goes in the dative: Анне нужно.
translation: Anna needs to leave work early.

s: Мой муж уже десять лет работает ___.
ex: Работать + instrumental for a profession: работать инженером, врачом.
translation: My husband has worked as an engineer for ten years.

s: С детства я интересуюсь ___ Древнего Рима.
ex: Интересоваться + instrumental. Feminine -ия → -ией.
translation: I've been interested in the history of Ancient Rome since childhood.

ex: Гордиться + instrumental. Дочь has an irregular plural stem дочер-; the literary instrumental plural is дочерьми (дочерями is colloquial).
translation: We are very proud of our daughters.

s: Вчера я встретился с ___ в кафе.
ex: С (with) + instrumental. Коллега declines like a feminine noun (-ой), but its adjective is masculine when it refers to a man: бывшим.
translation: Yesterday I met up with a former colleague at a café.
glosses: встретиться с: to meet up with

s: В субботу я случайно увидел ___ в торговом центре.
ex: Accusative animate masculine = genitive form: твоего брата.
translation: On Saturday I happened to see your brother at the mall.

ex: Accusative inanimate masculine = nominative form: новый стол. Only animate nouns change.
translation: We finally bought a new table for the kitchen.

s: На Новый год мы пригласили ___ на ужин.
ex: Animate plural nouns (any gender) have accusative = genitive: наших коллег.
translation: For New Year's we invited our colleagues to dinner.

ex: Feminine accusative: adjective -ую, noun -у. Animacy doesn't matter in the feminine singular.
translation: I really love nineteenth-century Russian literature.

s: В прошлом месяце мы наняли ___ английского.
ex: Accusative animate masculine = genitive: soft-stem -тель → -теля, adjective -ого.
translation: Last month we hired a new English teacher.

s: В нашей группе только два ___ из Москвы.
ex: After 2, 3, 4 (два, три, четыре): genitive singular: два студента.
translation: There are only two students from Moscow in our group.

ex: After 2–4: genitive singular года. After 5+ the form is лет: пять лет.
translation: I lived in Novosibirsk for three years.

ex: After 5–20 and round tens: genitive plural. Soft-stem masculine -ь → -ей: рублей.
translation: A bus ticket costs fifty rubles.

s: Моей сестре в мае исполнился двадцать один ___.
ex: Compound numerals ending in один take the nominative singular: двадцать один год.
translation: My sister turned twenty-one in May.

s: На столе лежат две ___ на английском.
ex: After две/три/четыре: genitive singular. Note две (feminine) instead of два.
translation: There are two books in English on the table.

s: В отделе продаж работают двадцать два ___.
ex: The last word of the numeral decides: ...два → genitive singular сотрудника.
translation: Twenty-two employees work in the sales department.

s: У меня два ___ и младшая сестра.
ex: With 2–4 and masculine nouns, the noun is genitive singular but the adjective is genitive plural: два старших брата.
translation: I have two older brothers and a younger sister.

s: На встрече мы говорили о пяти новых ___.
ex: In oblique cases the numeral and the noun agree in case: о пяти проектах (prepositional plural).
translation: At the meeting we talked about five new projects.

s: Я ___ поехать в отпуск в июле.
ex: Хотеть is mixed: singular like 1st conj with т→ч (хочу, хочешь, хочет), plural like 2nd conj (хотим, хотите, хотят).
translation: I want to go on vacation in July.

ex: Хотеть: the plural uses the 2nd-conjugation pattern with no т→ч change: хотим, хотите, хотят.
translation: We'd like to book a table for four.
glosses: заказать столик: to reserve a table

ex: Есть (to eat) is irregular: ем, ешь, ест, едим, едите, едят.
translation: What do you usually eat for breakfast?

s: Он редко ходит в рестораны, обычно он ___ дома.
ex: Есть: он ест. Don't confuse it with едет (from ехать, to go by vehicle).
translation: He rarely goes to restaurants; he usually eats at home.

ex: Дать is irregular: дам, дашь, даст, дадим, дадите, дадут.
translation: I'll let you know tomorrow morning.

s: Надеюсь, они ___ нам ответ в понедельник.
ex: Дать (perfective, future meaning): они дадут.
translation: I hope they'll give us an answer on Monday.

ex: Писать: с→ш in every form, 1st-conjugation endings: пишу, пишешь, пишет.
translation: Are you already writing the quarterly report?

ex: Мочь: г in я/они (могу, могут), ж in the other forms (можешь, может, можем, можете).
translation: She can only come after six.

s: Я никак не ___ найти ключи от квартиры.
ex: Мочь: я могу, они могут. The ж only appears in the ты/он/мы/вы forms.
translation: I just can't find my apartment keys.
glosses: никак не: just can't, in no way

ex: Платить is 2nd conj (-им, -ите, -ят). The т→ч change happens only in the я-form: плачу, платишь, платим.
translation: We almost always pay by card.

s: Сегодня я ___ за ужин, ты платил в прошлый раз.
ex: 2nd-conj verbs in -тить change т→ч only in the я-form: плачу. After ч write у, never ю.
translation: Today I'm paying for dinner; you paid last time.

s: Я ___ работать по утрам, пока все спят.
ex: Labial stems (б, п, в, м, ф) add л in the я-form of 2nd-conj verbs: люблю, любишь.
translation: I like to work in the mornings while everyone is asleep.

ex: Жить adds в to the stem: живу, живёшь, живёт, живут.
translation: He has lived in St. Petersburg for a long time.

s: Что ты обычно ___ по утрам: чай или кофе?
ex: Пить: the stem becomes пь-: пью, пьёшь, пьёт, пьём, пьёте, пьют (the same goes for бить, лить, шить).
translation: What do you usually drink in the morning: tea or coffee?

s: Я обычно ___ в семь, даже по выходным.
ex: Verbs in -авать (вставать, давать, узнавать) drop -ва- in the present: встаю, встаёшь.
translation: I usually get up at seven, even on weekends.

ex: Ждать drops the -а-: жду, ждёшь, ждёт, ждут.
translation: I'll be waiting for you at the main entrance.

ex: Verbs in -овать/-евать change the suffix to -у-: организую, организуешь, организуют.
translation: They organize this conference every year.

ex: Видеть is 2nd conj: вижу (д→ж only in the я-form), видишь, видит.
translation: Do you see that sign on the corner?

s: Сегодня я весь день ___ на совещаниях.
ex: Сидеть: д→ж in the я-form only: сижу, сидишь. Сяду comes from a different verb (сесть, to sit down).
translation: Today I'm stuck in meetings all day.

ex: Бежать is mixed: бегу, бежишь, бежит, бежим, бежите, бегут (г in я and они).
translation: Look, they're running for the train!

ex: Брать inserts е: беру, берёшь, берёт, берут.
translation: He always takes a taxi to the airport.

ex: Печь alternates к/ч: пеку, печёшь, печёт, печём, печёте, пекут (к in я and они only).
translation: How do you bake such a delicious pie?

s: Вчера я весь вечер ___ этот отчёт.
ex: A duration (весь вечер) points to the process, so use the imperfective: читал.
translation: Yesterday I spent the whole evening reading this report.

ex: A finished result that matters now (уже, ready to check) takes the perfective: написал.
translation: I've already written the letter; can you check it?

s: Каждое утро он ___ кофе по дороге на работу.
ex: Regular repeated actions (каждое утро) take the imperfective: покупает.
translation: Every morning he buys coffee on his way to work.

s: Пожалуйста, не ___ окно, здесь очень душно.
ex: A negative request (не + imperative) normally uses the imperfective: не закрывайте. Не + perfective imperative is only for warnings (не упади!).
translation: Please don't close the window, it's very stuffy in here.

s: Когда я ___ проект, я возьму отпуск.
ex: A one-time action that must finish before another future action takes the perfective future: когда закончу, возьму.
translation: When I finish the project, I'll take a vacation.
glosses: взять отпуск: to take time off

ex: A single future action with a result takes the perfective future: позвоню.
translation: I'll call you as soon as I land.

s: Он долго ___ эту задачу, но так и не смог.
ex: An attempt with no result (долго, так и не смог) takes the imperfective: решал.
translation: He worked on this problem for a long time but never managed to solve it.
glosses: так и не: never (in the end)

s: В прошлом году я начал ___ китайский.
ex: After начать, продолжать, закончить, перестать the infinitive is always imperfective.
translation: Last year I started learning Chinese.

s: Мне удалось ___ экзамен с первого раза.
ex: Удалось means the result was achieved, so use the perfective: сдать. (Сдавать экзамен = take; сдать = pass.)
translation: I managed to pass the exam on the first try.
glosses: с первого раза: on the first try

s: Не надо ___ хлеб, у нас ещё есть.
ex: Не надо/не нужно (no need to) + imperfective infinitive: не надо покупать.
translation: No need to buy bread, we still have some.

s: Я обычно ___ рано, но сегодня проспал.
ex: Обычно marks a habit, so use the imperfective present: встаю.
translation: I usually get up early, but today I overslept.

s: Пока тебя не было, к тебе ___ какой-то мужчина, но он уже ушёл.
ex: For a round trip whose result is gone (he came and left), use the imperfective past: приходил. Пришёл would mean he is still here.
translation: While you were out, some man came by to see you, but he's already left.

s: Можно я ___ твою ручку на минутку?
ex: A one-time request about the immediate future takes the perfective: возьму (from взять).
translation: Can I borrow your pen for a minute?

s: Каждый раз, когда он ___, мы ходим в театр.
ex: Каждый раз, когда... describes a repeated situation, so use the imperfective: приезжает.
translation: Every time he comes to visit, we go to the theater.

s: Сейчас я ___ в магазин, тебе что-нибудь купить?
ex: One direction, right now: use the unidirectional verb: иду.
translation: I'm heading to the store now; do you want me to get you anything?

ex: Regular trips there and back: use the multidirectional verb: ходим.
translation: Every Saturday we go to the pool.

s: Вчера я ___ в кино на новый фильм.
ex: A completed round trip in the past (went and came back) takes the multidirectional verb: ходил.
translation: Yesterday I went to the movies to see a new film.

s: Мой сын уже ___, хотя ему всего год.
ex: Ability, or movement in general, takes the multidirectional verb: ходит (he can walk).
translation: My son is already walking, even though he's only one.

ex: A specific bus coming right now, in one direction: идёт. Buses and trains 'walk' with идти/ходить.
translation: Look, there's our bus coming!

s: Завтра мы ___ в Казань на поезде.
ex: The present of a unidirectional verb can describe a planned future trip: завтра едем.
translation: Tomorrow we're going to Kazan by train.

s: Прошлым летом мы ___ на море, было чудесно.
ex: A completed past trip there and back takes the multidirectional verb: ездили.
translation: Last summer we went to the seaside; it was wonderful.

s: Когда я ___ на работу, я увидел аварию.
ex: Background action in progress, in one direction, takes the unidirectional verb: ехал.
translation: While I was driving to work, I saw an accident.

s: Сколько времени ___ до аэропорта на такси?
ex: A single trip in one direction (how long does it take to get there): ехать.
translation: How long does it take to get to the airport by taxi?

s: Помоги мне, пожалуйста, я ___ очень тяжёлую сумку.
ex: Carrying something right now in one direction takes the unidirectional verb: несу.
translation: Please help me, I'm carrying a very heavy bag.

ex: A skill or habit (knowing how to drive) takes the multidirectional verb: водит машину.
translation: He has been driving for twenty years.
glosses: водить машину: to drive a car

s: Мы ___ в Сочи, когда началась турбулентность.
ex: An action in progress in one direction, interrupted by an event: летели.
translation: We were flying to Sochi when the turbulence started.

s: Он ___ из офиса в шесть и пошёл домой.
ex: Вы- means out of: выйти из офиса. В- is into, при- is arrival, за- is a short stop.
translation: He left the office at six and went home.

s: По дороге домой я ___ в аптеку.
ex: За- means dropping in briefly on the way: зайти в аптеку.
translation: On my way home I stopped by the pharmacy.

s: Чтобы попасть в музей, нужно ___ через мост.
ex: Пере- means across: перейти через мост, перейти улицу.
translation: To get to the museum, you need to cross the bridge.

s: Наш самолёт ___ в семь утра, так что в аэропорту надо быть в пять.
ex: Вы- + летать means to take off or depart: самолёт вылетает в семь. При- means arrive, до- means reach, за- means fly in briefly.
translation: Our plane leaves at seven in the morning, so we need to be at the airport at five.

s: Мой коллега ___ в командировку в Самару.
ex: Travel to another city uses ехать-based verbs: уехать в командировку. Уехала would need a female subject.
translation: My colleague went on a business trip to Samara.

ex: Кухня takes на, not в: на кухне (in the kitchen). Где? → prepositional, -а/-я → -е.
translation: Mom is in the kitchen now.

ex: Где? → на + prepositional: на столе.
translation: The keys are on the table.

ex: Шкаф has a special location ending -у after в/на: в шкафу (but о шкафе, 'about the wardrobe').
translation: The coat is hanging in the wardrobe.

ex: Пол takes the special location ending -у: на полу. (В поле means 'in a field'!)
translation: The cat is sleeping on the floor.

ex: Угол loses its о (угл-) and takes the special location ending -у: в углу.
translation: The chair is standing in the corner.

ex: Гостиная (like ванная, прихожая) declines like an adjective: в гостиной.
translation: We're sitting in the living room.

ex: Положить (to put) answers куда? → на + accusative. Masculine things don't change: на стол.
translation: Put the keys on the table.

ex: Куда? → в + accusative: в холодильник. Compare где? → в холодильнике.
translation: Put the milk in the fridge.

ex: Куда? → на + accusative, -а → -у: на вешалку. Compare где? → на вешалке.
translation: Hang your coat on the coat rack.

ex: Куда? → на + accusative, -я → -ю: на кухню.
translation: Go to the kitchen, there's tea there.

s: Сними куртку и повесь её в ___.
ex: Куда? → в + accusative: в шкаф. The -у form (в шкафу) is only for где?
translation: Take off your jacket and hang it in the wardrobe.

ex: У (by, next to) takes the genitive: у двери. It works for both где? and куда?
translation: Put your shoes by the door.

ex: A shelf is a surface, so на: на полке.
translation: The cups are on the shelf.

ex: An oven is a box you put things inside, so в: в духовке.
translation: The chicken is in the oven.

ex: Кухня is the exception among rooms: на кухне. Other rooms take в: в комнате, в спальне, в ванной.
translation: We drink tea in the kitchen.

ex: Rooms take в: в комнате, в спальне, в гостиной (but на кухне).
translation: The kids are playing in the room.

ex: A balcony is an open platform, so на: на балконе.
translation: He drinks coffee on the balcony.

ex: Things hang on the surface of a wall: на стене.
translation: The picture is hanging on the wall.

ex: У + genitive means 'by, next to': у двери (by the door), у окна (by the window).
translation: The keys hang by the door.

ex: Дома = at home (где?). Домой = (to) home (куда?).
translation: I'm at home now.

ex: Пора домой (time to go home) is about direction, so домой.
translation: It's late, time to go home.

ex: Russian says plates, cups and glasses стоят (stand) on the table, even though plates are flat.
translation: The plates are on the table.

ex: Forks and knives lie flat: лежат.
translation: The forks and knives are on the table.

ex: Clothes on a hook or rack висят (hang).
translation: The coat is hanging on the coat rack.

ex: Shoes standing on the floor стоят.
translation: The boots are by the door.

ex: A phone lying flat лежит.
translation: The phone is on the sofa.

ex: Furniture and appliances стоят: холодильник стоит, шкаф стоит, диван стоит.
translation: The fridge is in the kitchen.

ex: Where something will hang → повесить (impf. вешать).
translation: Hang your coat on the coat rack.

ex: Things that will lie flat → положить (impf. класть).
translation: Put the forks on the table.

ex: Things that will stand upright → поставить (impf. ставить).
translation: Put the glass on the shelf.

s: Каждый вечер я ___ ключи на крючок.
ex: Repeated action (каждый вечер) → imperfective вешать: я вешаю.
translation: Every evening I hang my keys on the hook.

s: Куда ты ___ мои очки? Не могу их найти.
ex: One completed action whose result matters now (I can't find them) → perfective положить.
translation: Where did you put my glasses? I can't find them.

ex: A single concrete action after можно → perfective: помыть (or вымыть).
translation: Where can I wash my hands?

ex: Asking permission for one action → perfective снять.
translation: May I take off my shoes?

ex: A warm invitation to sit down uses the imperfective imperative: садитесь. Сидите means 'stay seated'.
translation: Come in, have a seat!

ex: День is masculine and the subject (nominative) → какой.
translation: What day is it today?

ex: Машина is feminine; у тебя (есть) машина — машина is the subject, nominative → какая.
translation: What kind of car do you have?

sub: prepositional (в / на / о): каком / какой / каких
ex: Где? в + prepositional. Страна is feminine → в какой стране.
translation: Which country do you live in?

ex: Ручка is feminine, the object of купил → accusative какую.
translation: Which pen did you buy?

sub: genitive (из / у / для / без): какого / какой / каких
ex: Для always takes the genitive. Подруга is feminine → для какой подруги.
translation: Which friend is this present for?

ex: Машина is feminine, the object of любишь → accusative какую.
translation: Which car do you like?

ex: With нравится the thing you like is the subject (nominative). Фрукт is masculine → какой.
translation: Which fruit do you like?

ex: With нравится the thing you like is nominative. Мясо is neuter → какое.
translation: What meat do you like?

ex: With нравится the thing you like is nominative. Страна is feminine → какая.
translation: Which country do you like?

ex: Собака is feminine, object of любишь → какую. (Feminine accusative is -ую for animals too.)
translation: Which dog do you love?

ex: Ресторан is masculine, the subject → какой.
translation: What's your favorite restaurant?

s: ___ город тебе больше нравится — Минск или Джексон?
ex: With нравится the thing you like is nominative. Город is masculine → какой.
translation: Which city do you like more, Minsk or Jackson?

ex: Число is neuter, the subject → какое. A set phrase: Какое сегодня число?
translation: What's the date today?

ex: Блюдо is neuter, the subject → какое.
translation: What's your signature dish?

ex: Погода is feminine, the subject → какая.
translation: What's the weather like today?

ex: With нравится the thing you like is nominative. Музыка is feminine → какая.
translation: What music do you like?

ex: Планы is plural, the subject → какие.
translation: What are your plans for the weekend?

ex: Plural subject → нравятся (not нравится) and какие.
translation: Which fruits do you like?

s: ___ брюки тебе нравятся — синие или чёрные?
ex: Брюки exists only in the plural → какие, and the verb is нравятся.
translation: Which trousers do you like, the blue or the black?

s: ___ деньги у тебя есть — доллары или рубли?
ex: Деньги is always plural. У тебя есть деньги → subject, nominative какие.
translation: What money do you have, dollars or rubles?

ex: Хлеб is masculine and not alive: accusative looks like nominative → какой.
translation: What bread did you buy?

ex: Кофе is masculine (an exception!). Object of будете, not alive → какой. (In casual speech you may hear какое кофе, but какой is the standard.)
translation: What coffee will you have?

ex: Язык is masculine, not alive → accusative = nominative: какой.
translation: Which language are you learning?

ex: Вино is neuter. Neuter accusative = nominative → какое.
translation: Which wine would you recommend?

ex: Молоко is neuter, object of покупаешь → какое.
translation: What milk do you usually buy?

ex: Музыка is feminine, object of слушаешь → какую.
translation: What music do you listen to?

ex: Книга is feminine, object of читаешь → какую.
translation: What book are you reading now?

ex: Plural, not alive: accusative = nominative → какие.
translation: Which languages do you know?

ex: Plural things: accusative = nominative → какие.
translation: What groceries did you buy at the store?

ex: Брюки is plural-only and not alive → accusative какие.
translation: Which trousers will you wear to church?

sub: prepositional (в / на / о): каком / какой / каких
ex: Где? в + prepositional. Город is masculine → в каком городе.
translation: Which city do you live in?

sub: prepositional (в / на / о): каком / какой / каких
ex: Где? на + prepositional. Этаж is masculine → на каком этаже.
translation: What floor is your office on?

sub: prepositional (в / на / о): каком / какой / каких
ex: Кафе is neuter (it never changes) → в каком кафе.
translation: Which café are we meeting at?

sub: prepositional (в / на / о): каком / какой / каких
s: В ___ церкви ты был в воскресенье?
ex: Где? в + prepositional. Церковь is feminine → в какой церкви.
translation: Which church were you at on Sunday?

sub: prepositional (в / на / о): каком / какой / каких
ex: Улица takes на. Prepositional feminine → на какой улице.
translation: What street is your house on?

sub: prepositional (в / на / о): каком / какой / каких
ex: Касса takes на. Prepositional feminine → на какой кассе.
translation: At which register can I pay by card?

sub: prepositional (в / на / о): каком / какой / каких
ex: О (about) takes the prepositional. Фильм is masculine → о каком фильме.
translation: Which film are you talking about?

sub: prepositional (в / на / о): каком / какой / каких
ex: Где? в + prepositional plural → в каких странах.
translation: Which countries have you been to?

sub: prepositional (в / на / о): каком / какой / каких
ex: Говорить на языке: на + prepositional. Plural → на каких языках.
translation: Which languages do you speak?

sub: prepositional (в / на / о): каком / какой / каких
s: В ___ брюках ты пойдёшь в церковь?
ex: В брюках = wearing trousers: в + prepositional plural → в каких брюках.
translation: Which trousers will you wear to church?

ex: Врач is masculine and a person: accusative = genitive → какого.
translation: Which doctor would you recommend?

s: ___ брата ты ждёшь — старшего или младшего?
ex: Брат is a masculine person: accusative = genitive → какого.
translation: Which brother are you waiting for, the older or the younger?

ex: Кот is a masculine animal: accusative = genitive → какого.
translation: Which cat do you want to take?

ex: Друзья are people: plural accusative = genitive → каких.
translation: Which friends did you invite to dinner?

ex: Животные are alive: plural accusative = genitive → каких.
translation: Which animals do you like?

sub: genitive (из / у / для / без): какого / какой / каких
ex: Из takes the genitive. Город is masculine → из какого города.
translation: Which city did you come from?

sub: genitive (из / у / для / без): какого / какой / каких
ex: У (at someone's) takes the genitive → у какого врача.
translation: Which doctor did you go to?

sub: genitive (из / у / для / без): какого / какой / каких
ex: Из takes the genitive. Мясо is neuter → из какого мяса.
translation: What meat is this soup made from?

sub: genitive (из / у / для / без): какого / какой / каких
ex: До takes the genitive. Число is neuter → до какого числа.
translation: By what date do I need to pay?

sub: genitive (из / у / для / без): какого / какой / каких
ex: Из takes the genitive. Страна is feminine → из какой страны.
translation: Which country is your friend from?

sub: genitive (из / у / для / без): какого / какой / каких
ex: У (by, next to) takes the genitive. Касса is feminine → у какой кассы.
translation: Which register has the shorter line?

sub: genitive (из / у / для / без): какого / какой / каких
ex: Нет takes the genitive. Plural → каких продуктов.
translation: Which groceries are we out of?

sub: genitive (из / у / для / без): какого / какой / каких
ex: Не хватает takes the genitive. Plural → каких документов.
translation: Which documents are missing?

sub: genitive (из / у / для / без): какого / какой / каких
ex: Для takes the genitive. Plural → для каких документов.
translation: Which documents need a stamp?

ex: К (to a person) takes the dative. Врач is masculine → к какому врачу.
translation: Which doctor are you going to?

ex: По takes the dative. Адрес is masculine → по какому адресу.
translation: What address are we going to?

ex: Подходить к + dative. Блюдо is neuter → к какому блюду.
translation: Which dish does this wine go with?

s: По ___ дороге лучше ехать в Минск?
ex: По takes the dative. Дорога is feminine → по какой дороге.
translation: Which road is it better to take to Minsk?

ex: Писать кому? → dative. Подруга is feminine → какой подруге.
translation: Which friend are you writing to?

ex: По + dative plural (on which days) → по каким дням.
translation: On which days is the store open?

s: По ___ праздникам ты ходишь в церковь?
ex: По + dative plural → по каким праздникам.
translation: On which holidays do you go to church?

s: С ___ другом ты ездил в Минск?
ex: С (with) takes the instrumental. Друг is masculine → с каким другом.
translation: Which friend did you go to Minsk with?

ex: Ездить чем? → instrumental. Транспорт is masculine → каким транспортом.
translation: How do you get to work? (what transport)

ex: С (with) takes the instrumental. Мясо is neuter → с каким мясом.
translation: What meat are these pies filled with?

ex: Платить чем? → instrumental. Карта is feminine → какой картой.
translation: Which card will you pay with?

ex: Работать над + instrumental. Задача is feminine → над какой задачей.
translation: Which task are you working on now?

ex: С (with) takes the instrumental. Plural → с какими программами.
translation: Which programs do you work with?

s: С ___ друзьями ты был в ресторане?
ex: С (with) takes the instrumental. Plural → с какими друзьями.
translation: Which friends were you at the restaurant with?

ex: Окно is neuter. Neuter accusative = nominative → какое.
translation: Which window can I open?

sub: prepositional (в / на / о): каком / какой / каких
ex: Где? в + prepositional. Здание is neuter → в каком здании.
translation: Which building is your office in?

sub: prepositional (в / на / о): каком / какой / каких
ex: На + prepositional. Место is neuter → на каком месте.
translation: Where (at what spot) are we meeting?

ex: По takes the dative. Расписание is neuter → по какому расписанию.
translation: What schedule does the bus run on?

ex: Звонить кому? → dative. Друг is masculine → какому другу.
translation: Which friend did you call?

ex: Перед takes the instrumental. Здание is neuter → перед каким зданием.
translation: Which building are we meeting in front of?
